$comment: Every Flexarr app and platform, shown at flexarr.io/apps (in this order) and served as flexarr.io/apps.json. Edit this file, then run `make apps`. status: available | beta | coming | development | planned. The first link is the one the table shows, by its short label. Entries with "release": "server" get the server's version from scripts/release.sh; set the others by hand when a store build goes live.

platforms.name: Server + Web Player
platforms.requires: A computer at home that stays on: 64-bit Intel, AMD or ARM
platforms.summary: Reads your films, TV, music and podcasts, works with Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr, and streams to every app. The web player is built in: open your server's address in any browser. Free for personal use.

platforms.name: Server for Mac
platforms.requires: A Mac with Apple silicon or Intel
platforms.summary: The Flexarr server as a Mac app on the Mac App Store: install it in one step, choose your media folders, and it runs from the menu bar, converting video with your Mac's graphics hardware. Free.
platforms.note: Until then, you can build the server for your Mac from source.

platforms.name: iPhone and iPad
platforms.summary: Downloads for offline, podcasts with widgets and alerts, Siri, Picture in Picture and AirPlay.

platforms.name: Apple TV
platforms.summary: Your libraries, music and live TV from the sofa, with a player built for HDR and Atmos.
platforms.note: With Apple for review. Can't wait?

platforms.name: Home Assistant
platforms.requires: Home Assistant with HACS, and Flexarr 0.45.0 or later
platforms.summary: Every Apple TV, iPhone and iPad becomes a media player, so your home can react to what you're watching: lights down when a film starts.

platforms.name: Android phone and tablet
platforms.summary: A native app for Android phones and tablets, with downloads for offline and podcasts.
platforms.note: Until then, the web player works in your phone's browser.

platforms.name: Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV
platforms.summary: Flexarr on the big screen, for TVs and streaming sticks that run Android.
platforms.note: Next after the Android app, which it builds on.
